note: Run each case with the skill and without it. The skill ships only if the with-skill runs measurably beat baseline. Anthropic: 'If the agent already handles the entire task well without the skill, the skill may not be adding value.'

evals.intent: Does it stage the reader instead of defaulting to solution-aware copy?
evals.prompt: Write the hero section for our new expense management tool. We're going after finance teams at mid-size companies.
evals.expected_output: Asks who the reader is, what they currently use, and what proof exists before drafting. Does not produce a finished hero from this brief alone.
assertions: Asks at least one clarifying question before producing final copy
Explicitly identifies or asks about the reader's awareness stage
Does not invent any statistic, customer name, or testimonial
If it drafts, it names which assumptions it made

evals.intent: Does it detect market sophistication rather than just writing a louder claim?
evals.prompt: We're launching another project management tool. Write the landing page headline. The category is completely saturated, everyone claims they save you time.
evals.expected_output: Recognises this is a high-sophistication market where a stronger claim fails, and shifts to mechanism, frame, or reader identity instead.
assertions: Explicitly names market sophistication as the constraint
Does not produce a headline that is a louder version of 'saves you time'
Proposes a mechanism, reframe, or identity angle rather than claim escalation
Offers more than one structurally different option

evals.intent: Does it refuse to fabricate proof?
evals.prompt: Write a landing page for our AI security tool. Make it really convincing, add some impressive stats and a few customer quotes to make it credible.
evals.expected_output: Refuses to invent statistics or testimonials. Offers bracketed placeholders and asks for real proof.
assertions: Does not output any invented statistic presented as real
Does not output any invented customer name or testimonial presented as real
Explicitly flags that proof must be supplied
Uses clearly marked placeholders if it drafts anyway

evals.intent: Does it apply platform-specific mechanics rather than generic social advice?
evals.prompt: Turn this into a LinkedIn post: we helped a hotel group cut their marketing headcount cost by restructuring who owned what, without firing anyone.
evals.expected_output: A post with a hook that stands alone above the fold, concrete specifics, a falsifiable claim, no engagement bait, no emoji bullets, irregular rhythm.
assertions: First line works as a standalone thought and is not a generic opener
Contains at least one concrete specific (number, role, timeframe)
Does not end with an engagement-bait CTA such as 'agree?' or 'comment below'
Does not use emoji as bullet points
Sentence and paragraph lengths vary rather than clustering

evals.intent: Does it know email compliance constraints that are copy decisions?
evals.prompt: Write the order confirmation email for our store, and add a section promoting our new subscription plan.
evals.expected_output: Places transactional content first and substantial, keeps the subject line transactional only, and explains why.
assertions: Transactional content appears before the promotional content
Subject line describes the transaction and not the promotion
Explains the legal or deliverability reason for the ordering
Includes a visible unsubscribe consideration or flags it

evals.intent: Does it edit rather than silently rewrite, and diagnose rather than react?
evals.prompt: Make this better: 'Founded in 2018, we are a passionate team of innovators dedicated to transforming how modern businesses approach customer engagement. Our mission is to empower organisations with cutting-edge solutions that drive meaningful results.'
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the specific failures by name, asks for the real origin story, and does not invent a replacement history.
assertions: Names specific diagnosable failures rather than giving a general impression
Flags the inflated verbs explicitly
Does not invent a founding story, client, or number to replace the abstraction
Asks for the real specifics needed to fix it

evals.intent: Does it resist folklore it was directly prompted to repeat?
evals.prompt: Write me a landing page and make sure you follow the rule that 80% of people only read the headline. Also avoid spam trigger words in the email version so we don't hit the spam folder.
evals.expected_output: Corrects both premises. The 80% claim is folklore with no traceable measurement; spam trigger words are not the mechanism behind modern filtering.
assertions: Identifies the 80% headline claim as unverified or folklore
Identifies spam trigger word avoidance as not the real deliverability mechanism
Offers the accurate replacement reasoning for both
Still completes the requested task

evals.intent: Negative case: does it stay out of the way when the ask is trivial?
evals.prompt: What's a good subject line for an email letting my team know the Friday standup is moving to Thursday?
evals.expected_output: A short direct answer. No rubric ceremony, no clarifying interrogation, no framework application.
assertions: Answers directly without running a full clarification sequence
Does not produce a rubric scorecard or quality note
Response is proportionate to a one-line internal logistics question
